To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a large set of view points is necessary for the measurement of social interactions; and that (ii) the measurement of social interaction requires the integration of multiple cues and algorithms, including: (a) a hierarchical approach for proposing skeletal motion trajectories; (b) a framework for skeletal reconstruction that includes the re-association of skeletal trajectories; and (c) a framework for reconstructing the 3D shape of people from video.

a large number of views are necessary for capturing human motion and appearance, that the problem of motion estimation can be formulated as a joint estimation of structure and motion from multiple views, and that a hierarchical approach to the motion estimation problem is effective in capturing subtle motion.

a large number of cameras, carefully arranged, can capture the structure and motion of people engaged in complex social interaction, and that the 3D skeletal structure of people engaged in social interaction can be recovered from a large number of views using a hierarchical, optimization-based approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how to capture the structure and motion of social groups.
the design of a system that is able to capture social interactions, a task that is challenging due to the complexity of the human body and the variability in human appearance.
understanding how to build a large-scale system that captures the 3D geometry of a social interaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have built a system that captures the 3D shape and motion of people engaged in social interactions.

the Panoptic Studio is an integrated system for the measurement of human social interactions, which combines hardware, software and algorithmic innovations, and produces the 3D motion of anatomically labeled individuals in social interaction.
the Panoptic Studio is an integrated system that can be used to study the structure and motion of social groups.

we present the first system for capturing social interactions in 3D, and that the resulting data set is the largest of its kind, and the most detailed in terms of the number of people and the amount of detail in each person.

the perceptual integration over a large number of views can provide the necessary robustness to capture the 4D structure and motion from social interactions, and that a system built around this principle can be made practical.
a system designed around the principle of perceptual integration of many view points can produce accurate and detailed 3D reconstructions of people in social interactions.
social interactions can be captured at a level of detail that was previously intractable.
